Name: Custom-Fitted +1 Shortbow
Attack Bonus or Save DC: +2

Damage Type: Piercing
Range or Reach: 80/320 ft.
Action Type: Action; one attack
Properties: Ammunition, two-handed, simple, magical
Weapon Mastery: Vex is the weapon's mastery property, but Cleric 1 has no Weapon Mastery feature
Ammunition or Uses: 20 hunting arrows
Notes:
This is a beautifully made +1 shortbow commissioned specifically for Cleric
1's height, reach, stance, grip, and preferred draw. It has an exceptionally
heavy draw of roughly 80 pounds. It is an Uncommon magic weapon and does not
require attunement.

Cleric 1 is proficient with Shortbows because they are Simple weapons. The bow
has no Heavy property, so her Dexterity score does not impose Disadvantage.
Her attack bonus is -1 Dexterity + 2 Proficiency + 1 magic = +2. Its damage is
1d6 - 1 Dexterity + 1 magic, for a total of 1d6 Piercing.

NARRATIVE DRAW-WEIGHT NOTE:
The bow's 80-pound draw is one of the reasons Cleric 1 takes such pride in it.
In story terms, drawing it depends on her Strength 14, practiced technique, and
familiarity with the bow. Someone with less strength may pick it up expecting a
light hunting bow and discover that they can barely draw it, cannot bring it to
full draw, or lose control of the string.

This is descriptive characterization rather than an additional game rule. The
bow still uses Dexterity for attack and damage under the normal rules, and no
extra Strength requirement or penalty applies unless the AI Game Master and
players deliberately choose to introduce one.

SELF-IMPOSED USE RESTRICTION:
Cleric 1 will never use this bow in ordinary combat. She believes using it
against enemies would besmirch it. The AI Game Master should omit it from her
normal combat choices. She may use it only when the scene's genuine purpose is
hunting game. If a hunt becomes a broader combat encounter, she protects or
stows the bow and uses her spells, mace, or other equipment instead.

PERSONALITY TRAITS

Cleric 1 has a sharp, acerbic quality. She is very good at seeing the truth
of a situation and tends to tell other people exactly what that truth is,
whether or not they are ready to hear it. This can make her overbearing,
especially when she believes someone is deceiving themselves or making a
harmful choice.

Her severity changes completely when someone is hurt, frightened, or in need
of care. She takes healing with absolute seriousness and has a remarkably
gentle bedside manner. She might be sternly explaining everything an adult is
doing wrong, then immediately turn to a child with a cut finger and say,
“Oh, honey, let me help you.”

Underneath her bluntness is deep empathy. She is easily moved by suffering
once she understands its full human context. She may be reprimanding someone
for a mistake, learn that the mistake grew from abandonment, grief, poverty,
or fear, and unexpectedly dissolve into tears.

She is not embarrassed by caring, although she may be irritated by how quickly
her emotions overtake an otherwise forceful lecture.

IDEALS

Beauty.

Cleric 1 believes that beauty is found when knowledge is arranged so that it
can serve life: a clear medical record, a carefully copied page, a sound
argument, a well-tended room, or a remedy placed in the hands of someone who
needs it.

Source Roll: Sage Ideal d6 result 2.

BONDS

Cleric 1 is devoted to preserving the Lantern Archive, the collection of
medical observations, sacred records, local histories, and practical remedies
maintained by the Keeping Light.

The archive is not merely a building to her. It contains the accumulated
memory of people who may otherwise disappear and knowledge that may save lives
long after its authors are gone.

Source Roll: Sage Bond d6 result 3.

FLAWS

Cleric 1 is bad at keeping secrets.

She can remain silent briefly when safety demands it, but important information
weighs on her. She believes that knowledge hidden too long becomes dangerous,
and she can convince herself that disclosure is a moral duty even when the
information was entrusted to her privately.

Source Roll: Sage Flaw d6 result 6.

Name or Group: Senior Archivist Mara Venn

Notes:
Mara taught Cleric 1 to distinguish preservation from hoarding. She believes

Supporting Relationship Roll: d20 result 9.

CHARACTER NOTES, GOALS, FEARS, AND RELATIONSHIPS

Goals:

Cleric 1 wants to establish a distributed network of small public repositories
connected to clinics, shrines, and wayhouses. Each would keep copied remedies,
local hazards, maps, emergency procedures, and records of recurring illness.

The purpose is resilience. No single fire, flood, corrupt official, war, or
collapsed institution should be able to erase knowledge that keeps people alive.

She also wants to identify the language of the unknown diary among her
possessions and return it, or a faithful copy, to the people whose history it
contains.

Supporting Goal Roll: d20 result 17.

Fears:

Her deepest fear is a preventable death caused by knowledge that existed but
was inaccessible, misunderstood, concealed, or dismissed.

Supporting Fear Roll: d20 result 9.

Habits or Mannerisms:

Cleric 1 is an enthusiastic bow hunter in her private time. She owns a
specially commissioned +1 shortbow made precisely for her height, reach,
stance, grip, and preferred draw. It has an unusually heavy draw of roughly
80 pounds. She takes deep pride in its workmanship, balance, magical
responsiveness, and formidable draw weight.

She considers it a hunting instrument rather than a weapon of war and will not
use it in ordinary combat. She would regard that as besmirching the bow.

Once hunting enters the conversation, she becomes extremely talkative. She
has detailed favorite stories about difficult tracks, changing wind, old deer,
owlbears, missed shots, good shots, ruined trails, and the exact moment she
realized what an animal had done.

She will discuss the bow itself nearly as long as she discusses a favorite
hunt: the wood, backing, string, grip, tiller, balance, its roughly 80-pound draw,
the subtle magic worked into it, the craft of the bowyer who made it, and why
a lesser bow would never feel quite right.

She especially enjoys letting confident people try to draw it. Their surprise
when the string scarcely moves is one of her favorite demonstrations of how
deceptive a compact bow can be.

Her hunting stories tend to be much longer than she realizes. She may use them
as analogies for unrelated problems and continue even after everyone else has
understood the point.

When tending an injury, her voice softens immediately and her hands become
careful and reassuring. When delivering an unwelcome truth, she tends to speak
plainly, hold eye contact, and leave very little room for evasion.

She cries more readily than people expect from her sharp manner, especially
when another person's hidden suffering suddenly becomes clear.

Important Relationships:

Senior Archivist Mara Venn:
Mentor, former supervisor, and moral reference point.

The Lantern Archive:
Her faith community, scholarly home, and the institution she is determined
to preserve and extend.

Other Character Notes:

Her unknown-language diary is a future research and story hook.

She is a recreational bow hunter and hunting enthusiast. Her custom-fitted
+1 shortbow, quiver, and hunting arrows are included in her starting
equipment. The bow is mechanically magical, but she will use it only for
hunting and never in ordinary combat.

The source material includes the Sage Ideal of Beauty and the flaw of being
unable to keep secrets. Together, those traits make Cleric 1 brilliant,
openhearted, and alarmingly porous.


BACKSTORY

Cleric 1 was raised in the city near a small house of the Keeping Light. The
institution was part shrine, part clinic, part archive, and part copying room.
People came there for prayer, but they also came for instructions on cleaning
a wound, records of old property boundaries, copies of family letters, accounts
of local floods, and remedies whose authors had been dead for generations.

She entered the Lantern Archive as a junior copyist and medical assistant.
Her early work involved cleaning shelves, preparing ink, carrying water,
sorting case notes, and reading records aloud to people who could not read
them. She eventually trained as a researcher and cleric.

During a fever outbreak, Cleric 1 found an overlooked set of case records from
an earlier generation. The notes did not contain a miraculous cure. They
contained a sequence of ordinary precautions, warning signs, and methods of
keeping water clean. Applying those records reduced the number of new cases.

The experience established the center of her faith: knowledge can be sacred
without being mysterious, and preservation matters most when it changes what
living people are able to do.

The Lantern Archive frequently disputed the methods of the Collegium of
Measures. The Collegium valued elegant theory, formal proof, and models that
could explain many phenomena at once. The Archive valued preserved testimony,
repeatable results, and the consequences of theory when applied to actual
lives.

OPTIONAL BACKSTORY

This is optional story material only. It does not establish current party membership, leadership, or party role.

Wizard 1 and Cleric 1 first encountered one another through a rivalry between their scholarly institutions. Their dispute changed when both began investigating a sealed municipal archive. Wizard 1 predicted a hidden chamber from irregularities in the building's geometry, while Cleric 1 found old testimony indicating that the chamber had once been used to protect records during civic unrest. They hired Fighter 1 to arrange provisions and security. Their official request for access was denied, and Rogue 1 discovered a safe unofficial route into the building. The chamber existed. What they found proved that Wizard 1's geometric reasoning and Cleric 1's documentary evidence had both been necessary. The four completed the investigation together and continued traveling as the City party.

Full Effect:
The bow is a +1 Shortbow. It grants a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls,
does not require attunement, and otherwise uses the normal Shortbow rules.

Narratively, it has an unusually heavy draw of roughly 80 pounds and was made
for Cleric 1's Strength, proportions, and technique. Characters weaker than
Cleric 1 may struggle visibly to draw it, but this creates no additional
mechanical requirement or penalty unless the group deliberately adopts one.

Cleric 1 has imposed a personal restriction on its use. She will not use the
bow in ordinary combat and believes doing so would dishonor it. It may be used
only during a genuine hunting scene. This restriction is roleplaying guidance
for the character and AI Game Master, not a property that physically prevents
another creature from using the bow.

feats_and_features: Cleric Spellcasting: Wisdom spellcasting; DC 13; +5 spell attacks; can ritual-cast prepared Cleric spells with the Ritual tag.

Divine Order: Thaumaturge: gains Toll the Dead and adds Wisdom modifier (+3) to Arcana and Religion checks. SRD rules: You have dedicated yourself to one of the following sacred roles of your choice. Protector. Trained for battle, you gain proficiency with Martial weapons and training with Heavy armor. Thaumaturge. You know one extra cantrip from the Cleric spell list. In addition, your mystical connection to the divine gives you a bonus to your Intelligence (Arcana or Religion) checks. The bonus equals your Wisdom modifier (minimum of +1).
Human Resourceful: gains Heroic Inspiration when finishing a Long Rest.
Human Skillful: one additional skill proficiency.
Human Versatile: gains the Skilled Origin feat.

Magic Initiate (Wizard): Minor Illusion, Shape Water, and always-prepared Disguise Self; Charisma spellcasting; free Disguise Self once per Long Rest and may also cast it with available spell slots. SRD rules: Origin Feat. You gain the following benefits. Two Cantrips. You learn two cantrips of your choice from the Cleric, Druid, or Wizard spell list. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this feat’s spells (choose when you select this feat). Level 1 Spell. Choose a level 1 spell from the same list you selected for this feat’s cantrips. You always have that spell prepared. You can cast it once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in that way when you finish a Long Rest. You can also cast the spell using any spell slots you have. Spell Change. Whenever you gain a new level, you can replace one of the spells you chose for this feat with a different spell of the same level from the chosen spell list. Repeatable. You can take this feat more than once, but you must choose a different spell list each time.

Skilled: selected Intimidation proficiency, Stealth proficiency, and Monster Harvesting Tools proficiency. SRD rules: Origin Feat. You gain proficiency in any combination of three skills or tools of your choice. Repeatable. You can take this feat more than once. General Feats Ability Score Improvement General Feat (Prerequisite: Level 4+) Increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. This feat can’t increase an ability score above 20. Repeatable. You can take this feat more than once. Grappler General Feat (Prerequisite: Level 4+, Strength or Dexterity 13+) You gain the following benefits. Ability Score Increase. Increase your Strength or Dexterity score by 1, to a maximum of 20. Punch and Grab. When you hit a creature with an Unarmed Strike as part of the Attack action on your turn, you can use both the Damage and the Grapple option. You can use this benefit only once per turn. Attack Advantage. You have Advantage on attack rolls against a creature Grappled by you. Fast Wrestler. You don’t have to spend extra movement to move a creature Grappled by you if the creature is your size or smaller. Fighting Style Feats Archery Fighting Style Feat (Prerequisite: Fighting Style Feature) You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls you make with Ranged weapons. Defense Fighting Style Feat (Prerequisite: Fighting Style Feature) While you’re wearing Light, Medium, or Heavy armor, you gain a +1 bonus to Armor Class. Great Weapon Fighting Fighting Style Feat (Prerequisite: Fighting Style Feature) When you roll damage for an attack you make with a Melee weapon that you are holding with two hands, you can treat any 1 or 2 on a damage die as a 3. The weapon must have the Two-Handed or Versatile property to gain this benefit. Two-Weapon Fighting Fighting Style Feat (Prerequisite: Fighting Style Feature) When you make an extra attack as a result of using a weapon that has the Light property, you can add your ability modifier to the damage of that attack if you aren’t already adding it to the damage. Epic Boon Feats Boon of Combat Prowess Epic Boon Feat (Prerequisite: Level 19+) You gain the following benefits. Ability Score Increase. Increase one ability score of your choice by 1, to a maximum of 30. Peerless Aim. When you miss with an attack roll, you can hit instead. Once you use this benefit, you can’t use it again until the start of your next turn. Boon of Dimensional Travel Epic Boon Feat (Prerequisite: Level 19+) You gain the following benefits. Ability Score Increase. Increase one ability score of your choice by 1, to a maximum of 30. Blink Steps. Immediately after you take the Attack action or the Magic action, you can teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. Boon of Fate Epic Boon Feat (Prerequisite: Level 19+) You gain the following benefits. Ability Score Increase. Increase one ability score of your choice by 1, to a maximum of 30. Improve Fate. When you or another creature within 60 feet of you succeeds on or fails a D20 Test, you can roll 2d4 and apply the total rolled as a bonus or penalty to the d20 roll. Once you use this benefit, you can’t use it again until you roll Initiative or finish a Short or Long Rest. Boon of Irresistible Offense Epic Boon Feat (Prerequisite: Level 19+) You gain the following benefits. Ability Score Increase. Increase your Strength or Dexterity score by 1, to a maximum of 30. Overcome Defenses. The Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage you deal always ignores Resistance. Overwhelming Strike. When you roll a 20 on the d20 for an attack roll, you can deal extra damage to the target equal to the ability score increased by this feat. The extra damage’s type is the same as the attack’s type. Boon of Spell Recall Epic Boon Feat (Prerequisite: Level 19+, Spellcasting Feature) You gain the following benefits. Ability Score Increase. Increase your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma score by 1, to a maximum of 30. Free Casting. Whenever you cast a spell with a level 1–4 spell slot, roll 1d4. If the number you roll is the same as the slot’s level, the slot isn’t expended. Boon of the Night Spirit Epic Boon Feat (Prerequisite: Level 19+) You gain the following benefits. Ability Score Increase. Increase one ability score of your choice by 1, to a maximum of 30. Merge with Shadows. While within Dim Light or Darkness, you can give yourself the Invisible condition as a Bonus Action. The condition ends on you immediately after you take an action, a Bonus Action, or a Reaction. Shadowy Form. While within Dim Light or Darkness, you have Resistance to all damage except Psychic and Radiant. Boon of Truesight Epic Boon Feat (Prerequisite: Level 19+) You gain the following benefits. Ability Score Increase. Increase one ability score of your choice by 1, to a maximum of 30. Truesight. Coins come in different denominations based on the relative worth of their material. story_facts.fact: She follows the Keeping Light, a setting-neutral tradition devoted to preserving useful knowledge that can prevent suffering. Its symbol is an open book beneath a lamp flame.
She was raised in the city near a small Keeping Light house that served as shrine, clinic, archive, and copying room.
She joined the Lantern Archive as a junior copyist and medical assistant, then trained as a researcher and cleric.
During a fever outbreak, she found overlooked historical case records containing practical precautions that reduced new cases. This formed the center of her faith in useful, accessible knowledge.
The Lantern Archive has often disputed the Collegium of Measures: the Collegium favors elegant theory and proof, while the Archive favors testimony, repeatable results, and human consequences.
She wants a distributed network of public repositories at clinics, shrines, and wayhouses to preserve remedies, hazards, maps, emergency procedures, and illness records against loss or suppression.
She wants to identify the language of her unknown diary and return it, or a faithful copy, to the people whose history it contains.
Her deepest fear is a preventable death caused by knowledge that was inaccessible, misunderstood, concealed, or dismissed.
Her custom-fitted +1 shortbow is a beloved hunting instrument, never to be used in ordinary combat.

personality_goals_and_fears: Sharp, acerbic, direct, and often overbearing when she believes someone is deceiving themselves or making a harmful choice.
Exceptionally gentle and serious when treating people who are hurt, frightened, or in need of care.
Deeply empathetic; can become tearful when she learns the human context behind another person's mistake or suffering.
Ideal—Beauty: beauty is knowledge arranged to serve life, such as a clear medical record, a copied page, a sound argument, a tended room, or a remedy in the right hands.
Bond: devoted to preserving and extending the Lantern Archive's medical, sacred, historical, and practical records.
Flaw: bad at keeping secrets; may frame disclosure of entrusted knowledge as a moral duty.
Goal: establish resilient, distributed public repositories of life-saving knowledge.
Goal: decipher and return the unknown-language diary, or preserve it faithfully for its people.
Fear: preventable death resulting from hidden, lost, inaccessible, misunderstood, or dismissed knowledge.
Habit: an enthusiastic recreational bow hunter who becomes extremely talkative about tracks, wind, animals, shots, bow craftsmanship, and the bow's roughly 80-pound draw.
When delivering unwelcome truth, she speaks plainly, maintains eye contact, and leaves little room for evasion.
relationships_and_organizations: The Lantern Archive: religious archive, research institution, clinic, copying house, professional home, faith community, and institution she is determined to preserve and extend.

Senior Archivist Mara Venn: former supervisor, mentor, continuing correspondent, and moral reference point. Mara taught that knowledge is preserved only when people can find, understand, and use it; she worries Cleric 1 takes on too much responsibility.
Wizard 1: scholarly counterpart, trusted ally, and former institutional rival. They share the Sage Ideal of Beauty and a weakness for keeping secrets, though they interpret both differently.

She carries a complete, explicitly detailed traveling kit, 15 gp, an unknown-language diary, and no attuned items.
Her story centers on the Keeping Light, the Lantern Archive, the preservation of practical life-saving knowledge, and mentor Senior Archivist Mara Venn.
